biggestGap: The r4 gap did not close: every resolvable droplet is still ONE convex analytic primitive — in the 12-60 px band 58.9% of our blobs fit a mathematically perfect ellipse to within 10% IoU (r4: 58.5%) against plate-01's 22.7%, and full convexity got WORSE (solidity>=0.95 on 28.0% of blobs, up from r4's 16.4%, against the plate's 10.3%) — because the new outline harmonic is a star-convex radial dent that can never produce a neck, a satellite or a pinched doublet, and it is multiplied to literally zero by defocus.
method_note: PREDECESSOR PROBE REPRODUCED EXACTLY. The r4 free-droplet probe (Rec.709 luma > 0.06, 8-connectivity, drop components with bbox width > 0.35*W or area > 1500 px) reproduces the r4 verdict's r3 AND r4 numbers bit-for-bit on all four frames: r3 15-fast 152/1623/med4.0/51.3%/21.1%/76.3%, r3 16-slow 128/1096/3.0/63.3%/15.6%/77.6%, r4 15-fast 82/311/3.0/76.8%/1.2%/13.8%/meanSat0.211, r4 16-slow 28/70/1.0/92.9%/7.1%/94.3%/0.703. Every number below is therefore like-for-like. HONEST DISCREPANCY: I could NOT bit-reproduce the r4 all-particle probe. Rebuilding it from its own description (high-pass lum - gaussian(sigma=5) > 0.030, minus largest CC of open(lum>0.15, disk 11) dilated 6) gives r4 15-fast n=204/px=3255 against their n=201/px=862; adding their own bbox/area cull to that mask gives n=203/px=1629. Their body mask must have differed slightly. I therefore FROZE MY variant (high-pass + body subtraction + the r4 bbox/area cull) and ran it identically over r3/r4/r4b/r5, and I quote r4 under MY probe so the deltas are real. Its conclusion is directionally identical to theirs. NEW PROBE for the r4 gap: per-blob ellipse fit (centroid + 2nd moments, area-matched) reporting IoU with the blob silhouette, plus convex-hull solidity, aspect CV and area tail, pooled over 8 fluid frames at 640 and over the 1280 hero, anchored against plate-01 LANCZOS-resampled to the SAME width so blob pixel areas are commensurate.

the_r4_gap_tested_directly_SELF_SIMILARI.reading: The report's claim that the harmonics 'reach pears, teardrops, peanuts and tri-lobed grains — shapes an ellipse fit cannot reach' is FALSE at the pixel level. An ellipse fit reaches 59% of our droplets to within 10% IoU, exactly as it did in r4, and the population became MORE convex, not less. The area tail also stayed at 4.5 p95/median against the plate's 8.3, so the size distribution is still not heavy-tailed enough. Only aspect variety moved toward the plate (CV 0.829 -> 0.507 vs plate 0.430).
the_r4_gap_tested_directly_SELF_SIMILARI.source_confirmation: /home/claude/juice/src/juice/fluid.js:583 `const lump = aS.y.mul(sharp)` with `sharp = 1 - flat` — the ONLY non-elliptical mechanism on the compact-drop branch is multiplied to zero as the drop defocuses, and every defocused drop is therefore an exact ellipse. Line 634: `R = max(1 - lump*clamp(H*0.62+0.5, 0, 1), 0.30)` is a purely INWARD, star-convex radial deformation about the particle centre, so at any amplitude the silhouette stays star-shaped about its own centroid: no concave neck, no satellite, no doublet, no pinch-off. Line 1344-1347 confirms the fattest and most resolvable class (rim beads) is authored `shape(0, ...)` — morph 0, i.e. always the compact branch, never the ligament branch, so the class the r4 critic actually counted never gets the interesting morphology at all.

evidence.visual_confirmation: Contact sheets of the 28 largest off-body blobs (/tmp/sheet-r5hero.png vs /tmp/sheet-plate1.png, 6x nearest-neighbour). r5: a grid of smooth dark-red convex lozenges, each with one soft pale bead, plus three pale streaks. Value variety is genuinely better than r4's grid of hot hard-edged red ellipses with a white pip, but it is the same OBJECT drawn at different tones. plate-01's equivalent tiles at the same pixel size are angular chunks, glassy multi-lobed transparent fragments, hard-edged specular slivers, strawberry pieces and cubes — no two of the same kind.

The r4 gap was 'a COUNTABLE field'; halving the count makes the field more countable, not less. r5's 04 dodges the identical-lozenge read mainly by having almost no juice left in frame at a beat that should still be wet. The builder attributes this to the stage lens energy conservation and declined to compensate per contract B4.5; that is procedurally correct and still costs the frame.

fix: One file, /home/claude/juice/src/juice/fluid.js, and it is still the droplet impostor — the amplitude of the shape variation is not the problem, its TOPOLOGY is. (1) Line 583: delete the `.mul(sharp)` from `const lump = aS.y.mul(sharp)`. The bokeh integration already smooths the outline by construction; multiplying the harmonic amplitude by (1-flat) on top of that deletes the only non-elliptical mechanism on exactly the droplets a viewer perceives as soft blobs, which is why frac_Sol>=0.95 went UP. (2) The structural change, in the `.Else()` compact-drop branch around lines 613-639: `R(theta) = 1 - lump*H` is star-convex about the particle centre and therefore CANNOT produce a concave neck at any amplitude. Add a second lobe and take the union: draw an offset centre `o = (q3, q4)` normalised to length `rr(0.55, 0.95)` and a satellite radius `rs = mix(0.35, 0.75, q1)`, then `qn = min(qn, length(c - o)/rs)`. Gate it on ~25-35% of the rim-bead class only (they are the resolvable ones, authored at line 1347 `shape(0, rr(0.16,0.44), ...)` — give them a morph value of e.g. 0.25 to select this branch) so mist stays round. Two overlapping discs at 0.55-0.95 separation give a real concave waist, which is a pinching doublet — the single most common silhouette in a real spray at 4-20 px and the one shape our field has never contained. Target, measured with the probe above on the 12-60 px band pooled over 02/03/04/05/09/10/16/07: frac_IoU>=0.90 from 58.9% down below 35%, frac_Solidity>=0.95 from 28.0% down below 15% (plate-01 sits at 22.7% and 10.3%). (3) Then restore the +250 ms mass: off-body particle pixels on 04-cut+250ms fell 6457 -> 3380. Per contract B4.5 the lever is not tint compensation, it is the rim/spray class LIFE tail — the `rng()*rng()` life draw at the rim-bead emitter.
